title: Stream-consistent failover controller for hosted API edge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a controller that enables graceful active-active failover across regional edges for streaming and long-lived HTTP/2 connections while preserving SLOs and minimizing client-side disruption. This work ties together routing control, circuit breakers, and coordinated load-shedding rules so hosted API customers experience predictable behavior during region degradation or overload.

Background: We currently have good request-level failover but streaming/session flows (HTTP/2 streams, websockets, long polling) either break or rely on client reconnect semantics that cause unacceptable replay/duplication for stateful workloads. Product SLOs require 99.9% availability for non-streaming requests and a 99.95% session continuity target (measured as reconnect-free duration for active streams). Engineering must provide a server-driven mechanism to: detect regional degradation, mark streams for graceful handoff or resume, open circuit breakers to protect stable regions, and apply prioritized load-shedding when capacity is constrained.

Goals: 1) Define and implement failover controller that coordinates between gateway routing plane and per-edge runtime to: shift new traffic, attempt graceful stream resumption, and limit blast radius for degraded region. 2) Add circuit breaker rules for edge CPU, queue wait times, and error-rate signals with per-customer granularity. 3) Implement multi-stage load shedding: priority-based admission, soft-queue head-drop for very long requests, and incremental model-cost based shedding. 4) Provide observability and runbooks for SRE/Support.

Non-goals: Full transparent cross-region stream handoff (stateful handoff) for arbitrary models. We will require resume tokens and short reconnects instead of live-preserve of open socket state for now.
acceptance_criteria: Failover controller can shift 100% of new traffic away from a degraded region per policy within configured cooldown (default 15s)
Streaming clients that implement resume tokens can reconnect and resume with no more than 2 seconds of progressed tokens lost for >= 95% of sessions during a controlled failover test
Circuit breaker trips when aggregated edge error-rate > 3% for 30s or CPU > 85% for 60s and remains open for configurable hold time
Load-shedding policy reduces overall token consumption by at least 30% under overload while keeping P0 customer traffic within SLOs
Automated chaos test (k6 + scablab) demonstrates controller actions and SLO compliance in a synthetic multi-region outage
design_decisions: Resume-token pattern: runtime will emit a small opaque resume token for streams every 5s; token encodes sequence number and last-completed KV checkpoint. Clients must present token on reconnect.
In-flight handoff: Instead of live socket migration, favor controlled disconnect + resume with a 2s grace window; implement backoff guidance in SDKs.
Circuit breaker signals: edge-level metrics (cpu, p99 queue wait, error-rate) plus per-customer error spike heuristics. Thresholds are tunable per-tier (free, standard, enterprise).

Load shedding: multi-tier policy: 1) per-route admission caps, 2) request-priority tagging (system, enterprise, free), 3) model-cost weight-based sampling, 4) soft-queue head-drop for requests exceeding X seconds of queue time.
Routing coordination: central controller writes route-policy changes to routing-config store (versioned) and edges subscribe; edges apply immediately to new connections and publish ack timeline.
Backward compatibility: non-resume clients will be redirected to best-effort fallback region but may experience a full reconnect; document SDK migration path.
rollout_plan: Prototype on staging: controller + edge changes + SDK resume token support (2 weeks)
Canary 5% traffic in us-east-1 -> us-west-2 scenario for 48h, monitor SLOs and error budget burn
Increase canary to 25% with synthetic streaming load tests (24h)
Full rollout to all hosted API regions after 7 days of stable metrics and green chaos runs
Follow-up: 30-day postmortem and tuning runbook updates
tasks: Implement routing-config versioning and subscribe/ack protocol (ENG infra change)
Edge runtime: emit and validate resume tokens; add soft-drop queue path
Controller: policy engine for circuit breakers and shedding rules
SDKs: expose resume token handling and reconnect helpers (node, python, go)
Observability: dashboards for session continuity, per-region circuit breaker state, shed rate, token-cost reduction
E2E tests: k6 scripts, scablab chaos job, and regression suite
